validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, FERC-jurisdictional project. Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, L.L.C. (a wholly-owned Kinder Morgan subsidiary) filed FERC pre-filing Nov 8, 2024, took FID Dec 19, 2024 (KM IR release, corroborated by Oil & Gas Journal), filed its certificate application June 30, 2025 (confirmed by Pipeline & Gas Journal's contemporaneous coverage and the EIA Aug-2026 record), and received FERC's certificate order July 31, 2026 under Docket No. CP25-514 (confirmed independently by KM's own Operations page and the EIA Aug-2026 release). This is unambiguously a real, actively-progressing project. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- a new-build, large-diameter (36in/42in), ~208-mile FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission mainline (not gathering, not distribution), consistent across every source. ATTRIBUTION: PipelineName 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline' (the parent TGP system) + SegmentName 'Mississippi Crossing (MSX)' matches how every source names the project ('Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company...Mississippi Crossing Project'/'MSX'); Operator and Owner (Kinder Morgan, 100%) both confirmed. LOCATION: Greenville, MS (Washington Co.) to Butler, AL (Choctaw Co.) confirmed by three independent sources down to the county level; the routes-repo geojson (P7802.geojson: PrjName 'Mississippi Crossing Pipeline', 206.0 mi, dia '36, 42', AffectedSt MS/AL, sourced to FERC Draft Resource Reports) is consistent with the sourced route and is not one of this batch's flagged route-vs-sheet mismatches -- no route action needed. SPEC ACCURACY: every spec cell (Fuel, PipelineType, Capacity, Length, Diameter, Location, SegmentCost, Start, Operator, Owner) checks out cleanly against 5+ independent, dated sources (KM's own FID release/Fact Sheet/FAQ/Operations page, EIA's Aug-2026 dated workbook, Oil & Gas Journal, Pipeline & Gas Journal, and Mississippi Free Press) -- see fills[] for the corroboration on each cell. The one caveat: the project's cost estimate has genuinely risen from $1.4B (at Dec-2024 FID) to the currently-recorded $1.7B (2025 filing-era estimate, which the sheet correctly reflects) -- a real historical escalation, not a sourcing conflict, noted on the SegmentCost fill.

validity.recommendation: P7802 should survive; P7841 'Mississippi Crossing Project' is very likely a duplicate filing of the same physical project and should be merged into / retired in favor of P7802 (or, at minimum, flagged so a human reviewer resolves the pair together).
validity.researcher_notes: Tested directly against the live GEM_gas_snapshot: P7802 (PipelineName 'Tennessee Gas Pipeline', SegmentName 'Mississippi Crossing (MSX)', sheet row 4182) and P7841 (PipelineName 'Mississippi Crossing Project', no SegmentName, sheet row per that PID's own worklist entry) carry IDENTICAL Status ('proposed'), Capacity (2100.00 MMcf/d), LengthKnown (208.00 mi), StartYear1 (2028), SegmentCost ($1,700,000,000), StartLocation/EndLocation (Greenville, MS -> Butler, AL) and StartState/EndState (Mississippi -> Alabama). Every independently-verified source found for P7802 in this pass (KM's IR release, Fact Sheet, FAQ, Operations page; the EIA Aug-2026 record; OGJ; PGJ; Mississippi Free Press) describes exactly ONE physical project answering to this description -- Tennessee Gas Pipeline's Mississippi Crossing (MSX) project, Docket CP25-514 -- never two. No second, distinct Greenville-to-Butler natural-gas project of this size was found anywhere. P7802 is the FULLER and more accurately attributed record: it carries the correct dual Diameter ('36, 42' in, matching every source) and a populated Operator (Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co LLC, itself independently sourced in this pass), whereas P7841 records only a single Diameter value ('42', missing the 36in lateral/mainline mix) and has no Operator or Owner populated on the operators/owners tab. This is consistent with P7841 being an earlier or less-complete duplicate entry for the same project (P7841's own LastUpdated per this batch's roster is 2025-10-16). Recommend P7802 survive as the canonical record; P7841 flagged for merge/retirement by whoever holds that PID in this batch (see cross_row_leads below).
